description: >
---

Run a swarm operation: the orchestrator is **code**, the expensive reasoning stays in the
**workers**, and routing/glue is **zero-token deterministic code**. See
`docs/AGENT_SWARM_ARCHITECTURE.md` for the architecture this skill operationalizes.

Usage: `/swarm PATTERN=<pattern> DATASET=<path|glob|list> [GOAL="..."] [AGENT=<name>] [RUBRIC=...] [STOP=...]`

Input: $ARGUMENTS

`PATTERN` ∈ `classify-and-act` · `fan-out-and-synthesize` · `adversarial-verification` ·
`generate-and-filter` · `tournament` · `loop-until-done`

## Steps

1. **Parse args.** `PATTERN` is required. Resolve `DATASET` to a concrete list of items (expand
   globs, split a list, or read a directory). Capture `GOAL` (held by the harness, NOT the
   workers — prevents "forgets goal"). If `PATTERN` is missing, ask which of the six shapes the
   task wants; do not guess.

2. **Build the harness (deterministic, zero-token).** Before any model call, fix the four
   control-flow concerns in code — never delegate them to a worker (§3.7):
   - **Order** — the stage sequence.
   - **Routing** — which item goes to which worker.
   - **Stop condition** — explicit, e.g. "every item processed", "judge picks one winner",
     `STOP` override, or a max-iteration cap. Never "until the model tires".
   - **Model choice** — tier per step (next step).

3. **Tier the models.** High-volume per-item work → cheap tier (`/ollama-spark` for EU-local /
   cost-free, or a small model); reasoning/merge/judge → Claude Sonnet; scoring / dedupe /
   inspection → **deterministic code**, no model. Spend frontier tokens only where reasoning is
   required (`AGENTS.md` Technology Stack).

4. **Execute the pattern:**

   | PATTERN | Procedure |
   | --- | --- |
   | `classify-and-act` | One worker labels each item's type → **code** routes each to the right agent/branch. Escalate only low-confidence items to a stronger model. |
   | `fan-out-and-synthesize` | One worker per item in parallel (`dws run <agent> --input` per item) → merge results **in code** into one structured table/report. Read *every* item. |
   | `adversarial-verification` | A **separate** worker checks the output against `RUBRIC` (or `quality-gate` agent). The generator never grades itself. Emit pass/fail + findings. |
   | `generate-and-filter` | Generate many candidates → **code** dedupes → keep survivors passing the predicate. |
   | `tournament` | Workers attempt the task different ways → a judge worker compares pairs/rounds until one wins. Generator ≠ judge. |
   | `loop-until-done` | Spawn workers, check the stop condition, **rerun only the failures** (not the whole batch), repeat until done or the iteration cap. |

5. **Aggregate in code → structured output.** Only structured results flow back, not full worker
   transcripts (keeps the orchestrator context bounded).

6. **Guardrails (§3.6, §8).** Point workers at the **governed ontology** (`ONTOLOGY.md` / LWM),
   not raw data — N workers reading ontology concepts reconcile at synthesize time and stay
   auditable; N workers reading raw databases multiply hallucination and leakage by N. Bounded
   iterations + timeout; per-agent cost budget; KYA-governed session; if any action is HIGH-risk,
   raise an HIL approval gate before acting. `loop-until-done` reruns failures only.

7. **Codification check (Skill Codification Rule).** If this same shape + dataset kind has been run
   before, say so and propose codifying it: set the `GOAL` once, save the procedure, and run it
   end to end via `/goal`. A swarm pattern reached for twice is a standing skill not yet written.

## Output format

```
SWARM: <PATTERN> over <N> items   [GOAL: <goal>]
Harness: order=<…> routing=<…> stop=<…> tiers=<cheap:…|reason:…|code:…>

Workers: <count> · model tiers used: <…>
Result:
  <structured table / ranked list / pass-fail + findings / winner>

Failures rerun: <n>   Iterations: <i>/<cap>
Cost: ~<eur>   Approval required: YES / NO
Codify? <suggested skill/goal, or "n/a — one-off">
```

## When NOT to use

- Single agent, one input → `/agent-run`.
- A pre-built named multi-agent pipeline (compliance-assessment, construction-full, seo-pipeline)
  → `/workflow`.
- Case coordination across domains/time with Themis → `/case-run`.
- Don't know which agent the workers should be → `/discover-agents` first.
